answer: Each spice jar is sealed and its scent written in the ledger, and the merchant sniffs the jar against the ledger before it may be sold. A juniper jar filled with dust fails the scent: at the garden of the sniff the spice must match the ledger's own description, and dust smells of nothing. Forging a jar means buying real spice, bribing a merchant and paying 10,400, while the quartz seal on the jar is broken if it is opened, so a jar whose scent was never recorded is thrown to the camels.
